things.name: the standard temple plan
things.who: developed in the New Kingdom from earlier models

things.name: temple orientation
things.who: mostly set by the Nile, with disputed astronomical alignments

things.name: the pylon
things.who: a gateway of two sloping towers, symbolising the horizon

things.name: temple columns
things.who: carved as plant forms to stand for the first marsh of creation

things.name: the daily temple ritual
things.who: performed by the priests three times a day, in the king's name

things.name: the temple priesthood
things.who: organised into rotating groups called phyles

things.name: the Canopus Decree
things.who: issued under Ptolemy III, adding a fifth phyle of priests

things.name: the bark processions
things.who: held on festival days, with the god's image carried in a boat-shaped shrine

things.name: the Opet Festival
things.who: lasting 11 days under Thutmose III and 27 days later; the annual journey of Amun, Mut and Khonsu from Karnak to Luxor, attested into the Roman period

things.name: the Beautiful Festival of the Valley
things.who: the annual crossing of Amun to the west bank, when families feasted in the tombs; the span is approximate, usually traced to Mentuhotep II and continuing well after the New Kingdom

things.name: oracles given by the bark
things.who: given as yes or no answers by the god's bark

things.name: the temple estates
things.who: endowed by the kings with land, people and livestock

things.name: the Wilbour Papyrus
things.who: a land survey of part of Middle Egypt, written in year 4 of Ramesses V

things.name: the temple wall decoration
things.who: carved and painted as relief, in horizontal registers

things.name: the temple sacred lakes
things.who: dug as purification pools standing for the primeval waters

things.name: the nilometers
things.who: built to measure the height of the Nile flood

things.name: the birth houses (mammisi)
things.who: built beside Late, Ptolemaic and Roman temples to celebrate the birth of the child god

things.name: the Ptolemaic temples
things.who: built by the Ptolemies as pharaohs, with Edfu begun in 237 BC and finished in 57 BC

things.name: the building of Edfu temple
things.who: built under Ptolemy III and later Ptolemies, finished under Ptolemy XII

things.name: the building of the Hathor temple at Dendera
things.who: begun under Ptolemy XII and hypostyle hall dated to Tiberius, decoration continued to Nero

things.name: the Roman takeover of Egypt
things.who: Egypt became a Roman province after Augustus defeated Cleopatra VII

things.name: the last monumental hieroglyphic inscriptions at Esna
things.who: carved under the emperor Decius, often cited as the last major hieroglyphic temple decoration

things.name: the first Christian bans on sacrifice
things.who: issued by Constantius II and Constans, but rarely enforced in Egypt

things.name: the Theodosian decrees against pagan worship
things.who: issued by Theodosius I, forbidding sacrifice and the worship of the old gods

things.name: the destruction of the Serapeum at Alexandria
things.who: destroyed in the conflict between pagans and Christians in Alexandria

things.name: the last hieroglyphic inscription at Philae
things.who: the last securely dated hieroglyphic inscription, carved by a priest of Isis

things.name: the last Demotic inscription at Philae
things.who: the last securely dated text of ancient Egyptian script

things.name: the closing of the temples of Philae
things.who: closed on the orders of Justinian I, carried out by his general Narses, according to Procopius; most sources say 535 to 537, one gives 553

things.name: the conversion of temples to churches
things.who: converted into churches and monasteries during the Christian period, over several centuries

people.name: Theodosius I
people.who: the Roman emperor whose laws of 391 and 392 banned pagan sacrifice
events: issued a further law against pagan worship

people.name: Justinian I
people.who: the Byzantine emperor said to have ordered the closing of the temples of Philae
